newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse's BUX tumbles, hit by H1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse's BUX tumbles, hit by H1 earnings.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange closed sharply lower on Monday, registering its biggest single daily fall in terms of points and the second in percentage.

The bourse was hit by earnings reports out on Monday and a setback on Wall Street on Friday, while it was unaffected by the latest batch of macroeconomic figures, released by the central bank and the statistical office on Friday and Monday.
The BUX index finished at 7,861.88 points, down 485.64 points and 5.82 percent. In late trading it was over six percent weaker.
"I think people are disappointed in the earnings," said James Oates, director for central and eastern Europe at UBS in London. "As a result they are marking down the whole market."
"The expectation of Hungary was that earnings should be better than expected," Oates said. "And in fact we have had a series of figures which (are) only so-so and indeed some weaker than expected."
Particularly pharmaceuticals Egis Gyogyszergyar caused disappointment, he said. Egis reported its first half after-tax profits falling to 3.033 billion forints from 3.314 billion forints.

Hotel firm Danubius and meat processor Pick were also among the five companies that released first half figures. Egis closed at 12,300 forints, down 900; Danubius at 6,220, down 385 and Pick at 15,780, down 320.

Analysts said Hungary's most recent macroeconomic figures, such as current account and trade figures released by the central bank on Friday, and the consumer price index by the central statistical office on Monday, were broadly in line with expectations, therefore left prices largely intact.
"It's clearly the company performance that is disappointing, the economic performance continues to improve generally," Oates said.
Frances Cloud, analyst at Nomura Equity Research in London said that the Wall Street's fall last week has contributed to today's plunge.
"What happened on Wall Street on Friday...that's one point," she said. "Another point is definitely these results, specially the Egis figures, which were clearly worse than anyone was expecting."
But Monday's fall also came as an aftermath of strong gains on the Budapest bourse, whose BUX index has more than doubled this year in forint terms.
"People are nervous, they feel the market ought to correct," Cloud said. "They are looking for anything that might lead them to believe it's going to correct."
A bourse official told Reuters that the BUX's largest fall in percentage terms occurred on February 3, 1994, when it slid 6.89 percent.
